checks.explanation: The selection disclosure is on page 1 and itemized prices begin on page 1, so it is on the same page as the prices.
No separate basic services line item with a price is listed; the basic fee is described as included in casket prices, so there is no includesText to assess for thinness.
No other mandatory charge for staff, facilities or overhead appears; listed fees are for specific goods or services that can be selected.
The embalming disclosure is on page 1 and the embalming price is on page 1, so it is on the same page.
No text states embalming is needed for direct cremation, immediate burial, or closed-casket service; the only embalming necessity language is the standard viewing example.
The alternative-container disclosure is on page 2 and the direct cremation price range is on page 2, so it is on the same page.
Direct cremation is offered with an option using a container provided by the purchaser, and no text says a casket is needed for cremation.
The direct cremation description lists what is included and no separate cash-advance crematory charge is shown, so there is no double-billing on the list.
Forwarding, receiving, direct cremation and immediate burial each have their own lines with prices, and other mentioned goods have priced lines.
No optional combination package is listed; forwarding, receiving, direct cremation and immediate burial are treated as required items, not packages.
No text asserts that a cemetery, crematory or other authority requires a purchase; only standard disclosure language about possible requirements appears.
No language about delaying decomposition or protecting the body from gravesite substances appears on the list.
No other wording undercuts the required statements, and the disclosures appear in standard readable form.
